name: Firebase Cloud Messaging
description: Firebase Cloud Messaging is Google's cross-platform service for sending notification and data messages to Apple, Android, and web applications. It supports individual device tokens, topics, conditions, delivery controls, analytics integrations, and high-scale fanout.
agentUseSummary: Add a dedicated service-account JSON for one Firebase project and bind one public-information topic; agents can publish one bounded title/body notification under Relay approval policy.

credentialRequirements.name: FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
credentialRequirements.label: FCM service-account JSON
credentialRequirements.helpText: Use a dedicated service account in the target Firebase project with only FCM send authority. Relay encrypts the JSON private key and mints short-lived messaging-scoped tokens.

credentialRequirements.name: FCM_TOPIC
credentialRequirements.label: Bound FCM topic
credentialRequirements.helpText: Enter one existing unprefixed topic intended only for public-information fanout.

capabilities.label: Publish to one FCM topic
capabilities.description: Send one title/body notification to the exact connection-bound topic.

approvalRequired.label: Publish FCM topic notification
approvalRequired.description: Send one bounded notification-only message to the exact bound topic.

blocked.label: Access devices, users, conditions, or subscriptions
blocked.description: Registration tokens, user identifiers, device groups, conditions, subscription management, and recipient inspection remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use arbitrary topics or payloads
blocked.description: Runtime topics, data payloads, images, links, analytics labels, platform overrides, TTL, priority, collapse keys, and custom options remain blocked.

blocked.label: Configure or administer Firebase
blocked.description: Projects, apps, IAM, service accounts, credentials, APNs/FCM configuration, templates, experiments, and administration remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw API or bulk access
blocked.description: Cross-project senders, arbitrary origins/paths/methods/headers/bodies, device batches, conditions, retries, SDKs, browser sessions, and exports remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Every topic fanout requires approval; identities, arbitrary targets/payloads, configuration, raw APIs, and bulk remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same one-topic fanout runs directly; project/topic binding, credential authority, content caps, audits, and provider limits remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw receives one fixed project/topic FCM notification wrapper with service-account token minting.
Hermes receives the same fixed project/topic FCM notification wrapper with service-account token minting.

providerSetup.blocker: FCM requires an enabled HTTP v1 API, configured client applications, a dedicated service account with messaging send authority, and an existing topic audience.
providerSetup.nextAction: A customer admin creates the least-privilege service account, provides its JSON and one verified public-information topic, then completes one approval-controlled live fanout test.

evidence.supports: Firebase documents service-account JSON, messaging-scoped short-lived OAuth tokens, fixed HTTP v1 project endpoint, notification payloads, and message-name acknowledgements.
Firebase documents topic fanout through HTTP v1 and warns accepted fanouts are fully committed and cannot be canceled.
Firebase recommends topic messaging for public information and documents fanout/subscription quotas.
Firebase documents trusted-server requirements, project IDs, short-lived service-account access tokens, and secret registration tokens.

securityNotes: The service-account JSON and topic are encrypted references; the private key is used only to mint one-hour messaging-scoped OAuth tokens at oauth2.googleapis.com.

Relay fixes POST https://fcm.googleapis.com/v1/projects/{credential-project}/messages:send and a single bound topic with notification title/body only; redirects are denied and responses capped at 1 MB.

Registration tokens, users, conditions, data payloads, images, links, platform overrides, subscriptions, project/IAM configuration, cross-project authority, SDK surfaces, retries, bulk, and exports remain blocked.
Safe mode requires approval because topic fanout cannot be canceled after acceptance; Dangerous mode removes only Relay per-action approval.
Provider-console setup, credential capture, IAM assignment, topic audience verification, and live acceptance remain customer/external steps.
